notes: Several failures from an unfamiliar IP are followed by a success from that same IP within a short period; flag for investigation, not as confirmed compromise.
A successful login from an unfamiliar IP without failures or other suspicious evidence should require review but must not be labelled confirmed suspicious solely because the IP is unfamiliar.
One failed attempt followed by a success from a known IP, with no other suspicious signals, should remain normal activity.
Repeated successful logins from a known IP without failure or other suspicious evidence should not be treated as suspicious just because there are several events.
Two known-IP failures followed by successes stay below the burst threshold and remain normal activity.
Three known-IP failures then successes are suspicious; known IP is context only and is not an automatic safety guarantee.
Known-IP successes plus one unfamiliar success without supporting failures remain insufficient evidence, not confirmed suspicious.
Failure burst followed by unfamiliar successes is suspicious; overlapping rule evidence is scored without runaway double-counting.
Three failures spaced hours apart fall outside the 30-minute burst window and do not alone justify a suspicious classification.
Shared failure evidence contributes once via GB-RULE-001 and once via GB-RULE-003; score remains capped at 100.
